concept.definition: A human decision with reasons and evidence about one acceptance criterion at a named specification version and result snapshot.
An immutable attempt to apply a change from one base snapshot, producing a result snapshot and check evidence.
An execution of tests with recorded command, environment, source snapshot, and outcome.
excludes: A test file that has never been run

concept.definition: A source document or code file addressed relative to one source snapshot.
excludes: Historical hunk path counted as a current file

concept.definition: A reviewable statement about the project that cites a source section.
A versioned constraint controlling indexing, access, review, or evidence release.
excludes: A retrieved passage that merely mentions a rule

concept.definition: A language-specific preferred or alternative expression for a concept.
A repeatable input and expected observation used to verify behavior.
excludes: A successful result from an unspecified run

concept.definition: A heading-scoped span of a source document with exact source lines.
excludes: A fabricated summary without source lines

concept.definition: A captured and identified set of source bytes and policies to which all evidence in a dataset refers.
excludes: A Git commit alone when working-tree bytes differ

concept.definition: A versioned statement of intended system behavior independent of implementation.
excludes: A claim that current code already satisfies it

concept.definition: A language parser's named code construct with a source range and stable join identity.
excludes: A vector chunk without a verified AST anchor

concept.definition: A checkable condition for accepting one requirement at a named snapshot.
excludes: A test result without its execution context

concept.definition: A typed and directed relationship between two identified objects with separate evidence and review state.
excludes: An untyped graph edge treated as proven meaning

concept.definition: A bounded and sanitized CKS response containing citations, bodies, graph neighbors, and integrity metadata.
excludes: Unreviewed semantic assertion treated as verified

concept.definition: A bounded source span represented by an embedding and searchable metadata.
excludes: A semantic fact proven only by similarity

concept.definition: A stable domain meaning with a definition, scope, aliases, and review status.
A named isolation boundary for source, indexes, reviews, and queries.
An origin, relative path, line range, file digest, and range digest tied to one source snapshot.
excludes: A similarity score without retrievable source

concept.definition: One immutable coordinated build of graph, vector, and optional semantic projections.

requirement.title: Safe ontology interpretation
requirement.statement: Optional concept matching preserves the existing hybrid retrieval candidates.

acceptance_criteria.given: An ambiguous term or an unverified concept relationship
acceptance_criteria.when: A user asks a natural-language question
acceptance_criteria.then: The baseline CKV and CKG citation set is preserved

requirement.title: Source-backed meaning
requirement.statement: Reviewed semantic relationships remain tied to one captured source snapshot.

acceptance_criteria.given: A relation with a code anchor from another snapshot
acceptance_criteria.then: Promotion fails and the active dataset remains unchanged

requirement.title: Filtered CKV recall
requirement.statement: CKV returns eligible nearest chunks under sparse metadata filters.

acceptance_criteria.given: A sparse filter leaves an exact-search-sized candidate set with at least K eligible chunks and many closer excluded chunks
acceptance_criteria.when: A filtered query requests K results
acceptance_criteria.then: The response contains K eligible chunks in exact distance order

acceptance_criteria.given: A larger filtered candidate set contains at least K eligible chunks
acceptance_criteria.when: A filtered query reaches a search budget or is cancelled
acceptance_criteria.then: The response marks incomplete with a reason and never claims K-result completeness
